question.text: Will the winner of the 2026 American League MVP Award be a unanimous selection?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the player announced as the 2026 American League Most Valuable Player (announcement scheduled for November 12, 2026) is listed first on every ballot in the official BBWAA tally, and No otherwise. Resolution is based on the BBWAA's official 2026 AL MVP announcement and its accompanying full ballot breakdown, published on and linked from the BBWAA Annual Awards page (https://bbwaa.com/awards). If that page is unavailable or does not report first-place vote totals, the official BBWAA vote count as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: The AL MVP is voted on by 30 BBWAA members (two writers from each of the 15 American League cities). If fewer than 30 ballots are included in the official tally, the question resolves Yes only if the winner is listed first on every ballot counted.

Witt led the AL in fWAR (6.6) and outs above average (22). Schlittler had a 1.94 ERA and 6.1 pitching fWAR. Martinez 2018) finished between 2nd and 4th. Alvarez had 6.2 fWAR at that point. [Yahoo](https://sports.yahoo.com/mlb/article/yordan-alvarez-vs-junior-caminero-for-al-mvp-can-a-designated-hitter-win-the-award-210931192.html)

- I could not find final 2026 fWAR or bWAR figures. If Witt or Schlittler finished ahead of Alvarez in WAR, that is a plausible reason for a stray first-place vote.

## 4. Base rates
These first-place counts are from my own memory and I did not check them this session:
- 2012-2025 AL MVPs: 4 of 14 were unanimous (2014 Trout, 2021 Ohtani, 2023 Ohtani, 2024 Judge), about 29%.
- Clear favorites who still fell short of unanimous: 2017 Altuve (27/30), 2018 Betts (28/30), 2022 Judge (28/30).
- Recent unanimous winners were usually also the clear WAR leader. Alvarez apparently was not the fWAR leader in late September.
- A primary DH has never won the AL MVP. Ohtani's unanimous 2024 NL win was a primary-DH season, so it's the closest precedent.
- In the MLB.com expert poll, 24% of voters didn't pick Alvarez first. That's a rough proxy only: it was a different panel, taken before the season ended.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Timing and what Yes requires.** About 10 days remain. The result is announced November 12, 2026, with BBWAA ballots published the same night. Yes requires the winner to be listed first on all 30 ballots, or on every ballot counted. Ballots were locked before the postseason, so nothing further can change the outcome. Only the reveal is left.

**(b) Status quo.** Alvarez very likely wins (Kalshi 96%). The open question is whether all 30 voters put him first. The default expectation for a DH with a late slump in a contested-WAR field is a lopsided but non-unanimous win.

**(c) Base rate.** AL MVPs from 2012 to 2025 were unanimous 4 of 14 times, about 29%.
- Restricted to clear favorites, the rate is roughly 40-50%. Altuve 2017, Betts 2018 and Judge 2022 were all heavy favorites who still fell short.
- Recent unanimous winners were almost always the clear WAR leader as well.

**(d) Key evidence.**
- For Yes:
  - Kalshi has Alvarez at 96% to win and 98% for the Hank Aaron Award (both 2026-11-02).
  - He led the majors in OBP, SLG and OPS, won the batting title, and his 179 wRC+ was 27 or more points clear of every other qualified AL hitter (MLB.com, 2026-09-22).
  - Ohtani's unanimous 2024 NL win as a primary DH shows a DH can sweep.
- For No:
  - The MLB.com expert poll (2026-09-22) had 9 of 38 experts not picking Alvarez first: Caminero 7, Witt 1, Schlittler 1.
  - Alvarez slumped to an .840 OPS over his last 41 games.
  - Witt led the AL in fWAR (6.6) and outs above average.
  - Schlittler had a 1.94 ERA and 6.1 fWAR.
  - Caminero matched Alvarez's 42 home runs.
  - Alvarez is a DH without Ohtani's two-way premium.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: Alvarez wins with something like 25 of 30 first-place votes, with one or two WAR-focused voters choosing Witt and a couple going for Caminero or Schlittler. This is the likely outcome.
- Yes: voters treat his huge wRC+ lead and the triple-slash titles as decisive, all 30 put him first, and the expert poll's dissent turns out to reflect pre-season-end noise.

**(f) Adjustment.** I start from about 40% for a clear favorite. Several factors push that down:
- He was not the WAR leader.
- He is a pure DH.
- He slumped late.
- About a quarter of an expert panel dissented.

Any one dissenting vote among 30 resolves No. I move down to about 13%.

Probability: 13%

(a) The outcome will be known on 2026-11-12, about 10 days from now, when the BBWAA posts its ballot breakdown. For Yes, the announced AL MVP, almost certainly Yordan Alvarez, must be listed first on all 30 ballots. Ballots were locked before the postseason, so the result is already fixed and simply not yet public.

(b) Status quo: nothing is settled. The default for any race is non-unanimity, because one dissenting writer out of 30 is enough to produce No.

(c) Base rate: from 2012 to 2025, 4 of 14 AL MVPs were unanimous, about 29%. If I narrow the reference class to heavy favorites (roughly 90% or better to win), the rate is about 45-50%. In that group, Trout 2014, Ohtani 2021 and 2023, and Judge 2024 were unanimous, while Altuve 2017, Betts 2018 and Judge 2022 each lost two or three first-place votes. The unanimous winners were nearly always the clear WAR leader and had no positional discount.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Kalshi had Alvarez at 0.96 to win on 2026-11-02, and the Hank Aaron Award market at 0.98, which points to a lopsided race.
  - Alvarez's 179 wRC+ was at least 27 points ahead of any other qualified AL hitter (MLB.com, 2026-09-22).
  - He led the majors in OBP, slugging and OPS.
- **For No:**
  - In the MLB.com expert poll on 2026-09-22, 9 of 38 panelists (24%) did not pick Alvarez first, and 7 of those chose Caminero.
  - Alvarez slumped late, hitting .264 with an .840 OPS over his last 41 games.
  - Witt led the AL in fWAR (6.6) and outs above average in late September.
  - Schlittler posted a 1.94 ERA with 6.1 fWAR, which gives voters who prefer pitchers an alternative.
  - Alvarez is a primary DH. No primary DH has ever won the AL MVP, which signals that some voters discount the position.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** Two writers who weight WAR heavily put Witt first, citing his league-leading fWAR and defense, and one writer puts Caminero first for his 42 home runs plus third-base defense. Alvarez wins with 27 first-place votes.
- **Yes:** Writers treat the lead in rate stats and wRC+ as decisive, as with Ohtani's unanimous 2024 NL MVP as a DH, and all 30 put Alvarez first.

(f) Reasoning: I start from about 45%, the rate for heavy favorites. I move down sharply for three reasons:
- The expert panel showed 24% dissent. With a per-voter dissent rate even near 5-10%, the chance that all 30 BBWAA writers agree falls well under 20%.
- Alvarez was not the WAR leader.
- He carries the DH discount and slumped late.

The win market is very confident, but that is about winning, not about unanimity. Final estimate: around 14%.

Probability: 14%

(a) **Time left and what Yes requires.** The result will be known around November 12-13, 2026, about 10 days away. For Yes, the announced 2026 AL MVP must be first on all 30 BBWAA ballots, with zero first-place votes going to anyone else. Ballots are already locked.

(b) **Status quo.** Alvarez is the overwhelming favorite to win (Kalshi 0.96). However, "winning" is not the same as "unanimous." By default, a lopsided win with a few scattered first-place votes elsewhere is the most likely outcome.

(c) **Base rate.** About 4 of 14 AL MVPs from 2012 to 2025 were unanimous, roughly 29%. These counts are from memory and were not checked this session. Restricted to clear favorites, the rate is higher, maybe 40-50%. But the unanimous cases (Trout 2014, Ohtani 2021 and 2023, Judge 2024) were also clear WAR leaders, often with historic seasons. Clear favorites without that WAR edge (Altuve 2017, Betts 2018, Judge 2022) often lost 2 or 3 first-place votes.

(d) **Strongest evidence.**
- For Yes:
  - Alvarez led MLB in OBP, SLG, OPS and walks, won the batting title, and had a 179 wRC+ at least 27 points ahead of any other AL hitter (MLB.com, Sept 22).
  - The markets price him at 96-98% for the MVP and the Hank Aaron Award.
  - Ohtani's unanimous 2024 NL MVP shows a primary DH can sweep.
- For No:
  - In MLB.com's Sept 22 poll, 9 of 38 experts (24%) picked someone other than Alvarez: Caminero 7, Witt 1, Schlittler 1.
  - Alvarez slumped late (.840 OPS over his last 41 games).
  - Witt led the AL in fWAR (6.6) and outs above average.
  - Schlittler posted a 1.94 ERA with 6.1 fWAR.
  - Caminero tied Alvarez with 42 HR, and Alonso led the AL with 43.
  - Alvarez is a primary DH, a profile no AL MVP has ever had, and some voters discount it.
  - Even if each voter had only a 5% chance of deviating, 0.95^30 ≈ 21%. The poll implies far more dispersion than that.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- No: Alvarez wins with roughly 22-27 first-place votes. Caminero picks up a few from voters who weight his counting stats and defense, and one WAR-focused voter picks Witt or Schlittler.
- Yes: The writers view Alvarez's rate-stat dominance as decisive, as they did with Ohtani in 2024, and all 30 put him first, with the expert-poll dissent not carrying over to the actual electorate.

(f) **From base rate to forecast.** I start near the 29% base rate. I move down substantially for three reasons: Alvarez was not the WAR leader, he is a DH, he slumped late, and the expert panel showed 24% dissent. That last point implies a very low chance of zero dissenters among 30 voters, even allowing that the BBWAA electorate may be more consolidated than the poll. That puts me at roughly 7-9%.

Probability: 8%

(a) About 10 days remain. The result comes out November 12, 2026, with the BBWAA ballot breakdown published that night. For Yes, the announced AL MVP, almost certainly Yordan Alvarez, must be listed first on all 30 ballots.

(b) No result exists yet. The status quo is Alvarez winning, but with a split first-place vote, which resolves No. The best current snapshot is MLB.com's expert poll, where Alvarez got 29 of 38 first-place votes.

(c) Base rate: 3 of the last 5 AL MVPs were unanimous (60%). Each unanimous winner, though, was historically dominant with no close WAR rival. Among winners who faced a real rival or an expert poll split near 75%, as in 2022 and 2025, unanimity was 0 of 2. For races with a contested profile like this one, I estimate a 10-15% base rate.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Kalshi has Alvarez at 96% to win and 98% for the Hank Aaron Award (Nov 2).
  - He led the majors in OBP, SLG, OPS and walks, won the batting title and led the AL in offensive WAR.
  - BBWAA voters tend to converge more than expert polls do.
- **For No:**
  - MLB.com's final poll (Sept 22) gave 9 of 38 first-place votes to others: Caminero 7, Witt 1, Schlittler 1.
  - Alvarez and Witt were tied for the AL lead in FanGraphs WAR at 6.8 (Sept 27).
  - Alvarez is a primary DH, and the Astros finished .500.
